sources.notes: 417 models at 687,878 bytes on 2026-08-26, re-probed at 687,941, so no size equality is asserted anywhere. minBytes is half the recorded size and minRecords 300 is a floor well under the 417 observed. Fast tier because cache-control gives a 300s TTL, and 15 minutes sits above that floor with headroom for edge age skew. Freshness kind none: this is a live catalogue, not a feed, and its own bytes drift between probes.

Predicate is extracted, not bytes, because two reviewers measured three per-request volatile regions independently and hours apart: a provisional userId UUIDv7 whose embedded ms timestamp decodes to the fetch instant, a 37 to 41 key posthogFlags map that re-rolls on any request because the visitor is anonymous, and a window.__CF$cv$params blob carrying the request's own cf-ray and clock, which changes on every response by construction. Masking only the first leaves the bodies unequal, so the predicate would fire every run and commit 5.2 MB forever into a history that is never rewritten. A mask list keyed on flag names also rots as arena ships experiments, so the predicate extracts the (publicName, displayName, rating, votes) tuples instead. Status is pending until the arena extractor exists. Size is per-request volatile too (5,235,684 to 5,235,774 observed), so minBytes is half the smaller observation and no fixed size is asserted. Freshness content/30 rather than the usual 90: the leaderboard gained models across both probe sessions and codename reveals are the entire point, so a quiet month means the extractor broke rather than that the industry stopped shipping. timeoutS 120 for a 5.2 MB body.

Pending. Per-request volatile, measured 2026-08-26: two fetches 4 seconds apart differ in 24 of 516 lastmod values while the loc set is identical, and the values oscillate backwards, which is two live edge-cache generations rather than a rebuild. Task 8 gives it sitemapDated, NOT sitemapLoc: keying on the loc set alone reduces this source to add/remove detection, and its per-URL lastmod is the thing that makes edits detectable. sitemapDated keeps every lastmod except those shared by three or more URLs at the same millisecond, which is the build stamp. Do not reactivate before that predicate exists; under bytes this commits 67 KB every run.

The forecasting artifact. 13,410 bytes for the .md twin against 1,006,482 for the HTML page, which is why the .md URL is the archived one; minBytes is half the 13,410. contentType text because a markdown parse check is exactly as vacuous as a plain text one, so the canary carries the health check here. Non-numeric families exist (claude-fable-5, claude-mythos-preview), so no claude-(opus|sonnet|haiku)-N regex anywhere downstream. Eight or more further tables follow the master one.
63,970 bytes on 2026-08-26, so minBytes is half that. The llms-full.txt twin is excluded deliberately at 39,763,086 bytes per day.

66,545 bytes when spec section 4 was probed on 2026-08-26, so minBytes is half that; a second probe the same day read 69,285, so this file drifts and no size equality is asserted anywhere. The /docs/ path is load bearing and the two files were measured side by side on 2026-08-26: openrouter.ai/docs/llms.txt is 69,285 bytes, md5 32a32f3aa92fae497c7addebe303c6c7, opening '# OpenRouter | Documentation', while openrouter.ai/llms.txt is 72,739 bytes, md5 2a015c6c8ae672e20cac55541a96f38e, opening '# OpenRouter'. Different files, not a redirect.

Predicate is extracted over the <loc> set only. This sitemap is not static: cache-control is public, max-age=0, must-revalidate and cf-cache-status is DYNAMIC. It is rebuilt several times a day, rewriting about 100 <lastmod> values per rebuild independent of any content change, so a bytes predicate would commit 617 KB of build noise every run into a history that is never rewritten. Status is pending until the sitemapLoc extractor exists. This is the same treatment already given to platform.claude.com/sitemap.xml. retries 3 rather than the usual 2 because a curl (35) connection reset was observed live on this host. 616,687 bytes and 5,051 <url> elements recorded on 2026-08-26, so minBytes is half the byte figure; minRecords stays null until something counts sitemap entries.

34,432 bytes on 2026-08-26, so minBytes is half that. This host is deliberate and unobvious: platform.openai.com/llms.txt 404s, and platform.openai.com/docs/llms.txt is a 301 to this URL whose own 81-byte body is the redirect text, which a collector that does not follow redirects would archive instead of the file. That 81-byte body is caught by minBytes and by the size band, never by parsing.

797,252 bytes on 2026-08-26, so minBytes is half that, and timeoutS 90 rather than 60 for the size. This is the full-text file rather than an index because Groq ships zero .md twins, so it is the only path to Groq content diffs. That also makes it the source the proportional hold rule exists for: one Groq docs-platform migration is a whole-file rewrite with nothing to threshold on.

Predicate is extracted over sorted table blocks. bytes is wrong here because the file's rows re-permute per request, so it would commit 1.46 MB of pure permutation daily forever, and mask cannot express it because reordering is not a maskable substring. Sorting in the deriver cannot fix it either: the deriver only ever sees what was committed, and the commit decision is upstream of it, so the predicate itself has to express sort equality. The sorted md5 b92fafe614002915ea5a5b5e5be3060b reproduced across three independent captures hours apart while every raw md5 differed. Of the two conflicting magnitude measurements the narrower one is adopted (about 12 changed lines and 270 differing bytes across 6 runs, adjacent row swaps in two tables), because it is the only one with a byte count attached and it argues for sorting within table blocks rather than across the whole file, which preserves the deriver's ability to see a legitimate section reorder. Status is pending until the xai extractor exists. 1,465,407 bytes recorded on 2026-08-26, so minBytes is half that, and timeoutS 120 for the size. No llms-full twin exists.

The repository is anomalyco/models.dev, not sst/models.dev. 20 entries, 20,239 bytes, no API rate limit, so minBytes is half the recorded size. The observed 20-entry window spanned 24m29s, so a daily poll loses commits and even a fast tier could; O3 resolves that with git fetch rather than a tier move, which is why this stays daily. freshness feed/7 rather than the incident feeds' 120 because this is an activity feed that cycles its whole window in under half an hour, so a week of silence means the feed or the repo is dead, not that the project is quiet. sizeBand widened to [0.4, 3.0] because a fixed count window of 20 commits sizes with how verbose the messages are, which is not a content integrity signal.

25 entries, all carrying <published>, newest 2026-08-24T20:26:21Z. Downstream must key on published and not updated: 16 of the 25 share a bulk backfill updated of 2026-08-14. freshness feed/120 because a provider with a genuinely good quarter publishes no incidents for 60+ days, and a daily failure mail for that is how alerting channels get muted; a stale feed is stale, not failed, and does not drive the exit code. Spec section 4 records entry counts but no byte size for this feed, so minBytes is deliberately a stub catcher at 1,024 bytes, which an empty or error body cannot clear, rather than an invented figure dressed up as a measurement; the real number lands when Task 6 captures the fixture. sizeBand widened to [0.4, 3.0] for the same reason as modelsdev-commits: one long post mortem entering or leaving a fixed 25 entry window moves total bytes more than a 2x band tolerates.

Pending. Per-request volatile, measured 2026-08-26: six fetches gave two distinct md5s at an identical 92,282 bytes. The feed-level updated re-stamps per cache generation and the component list inside every entry is permuted, 493 differing runs across 15,600 bytes, while entry id order and set stay stable. Task 8 gives it atomStatus: each entry's id, its updated, and its component list SORTED, so the permutation dies while a component appearing or vanishing is still detected, which is the quiet withdrawal a status feed exists to leak. This feed also carries zero published elements, only updated, so it must not share date handling with claude-status. Do not reactivate before that predicate exists; under bytes this commits 92 KB every run.
